messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Canary group 'canary-east-1' failing health checks (error-rate spike + latency). Pager sent to #incidents and @sam_oncall.
sam_oncall: on it. pulling up dashboards now — what are the symptoms?
maya_sre: seeing p95 jump from 220ms -> 1.2s and 5xx rate ~7% on the canary shard, non-canary unchanged. Affected routes: /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings.
ryan_release: can confirm. This started approx 2m after the canary rollout reached 10% traffic. Auto-rollback didn't fire; looks like the rollout policy's "error_threshold" was 10% and we hit ~7% so it stayed.
sam_oncall: ok we'll do manual rollback and kill the feature flag. @deploy-bot can you pause traffic to canary?
deploy-bot: running: `deployctl traffic shift --group canary-east-1 --to 0% --reason "incident/1728374123"`
ops-bot: traffic shift initiated, draining connections. ETA ~90s.
julie_support: flagging CS to prep inbound messages for any customers contacting support. which orgs are showing errors?
maya_sre: query: `select org_id, count(*) from request_logs where canary=true and status >= 500 group by org_id order by 2 desc limit 5;` returns orgs: AcmeCorp (34%), BetaCo (18%), internal-infra-tests (12%). total impacted ~2.1k requests in last 5m.
ryan_release: initiating rollback: `deployctl rollback --group canary-east-1 --to revision:stable-2026-03-07 --force`
deploy-bot: rollback job started (job id: jb_94123). streaming logs: "graceful drain, shutting down workers, unmounting model cache..."
sam_oncall: while rollback runs, flip kill-switch for the new prefetch cache feature: `ffctl set prefetch_cache_enabled false --env canary` — this avoids recurrence on re-drain.
ryan_release: done. command output: "featureflag prefetch_cache_enabled set to false for canary"
maya_sre: watchlist: KV cache pressure may cause slow recovery; probing the model nodes for OOMs. logs show repeated GC stalls on two canary hosts.
sam_oncall: good catch. I'm marking those instances for termination after rollback completes.
ops-bot: rollback reached 60% -> 100% for group canary-east-1. All canary instances replaced with stable revision.
deploy-bot: post-rollback smoke checks: `curl -sS https://canary-check.internal/v1/health` -> {"ok":true}, latency p95 ~210ms.
maya_sre: metrics look good: 5xx drops back to ~0.2%, p95 back to baseline. No new OOM events after model cache disabled.
julie_support: sending support note draft: "We observed elevated error rates for a subset of Canaries after a recent canary rollout. We rolled back the canary and disabled a prefetch cache feature; services are healthy. If you saw errors, please share request IDs and timestamps." Want me to push to status page?
sam_oncall: yes post an incident update (no customer-facing outage, localized canary impact). cc @julie_support for tone.
ryan_release: quick verification: smoke script against AcmeCorp tenant endpoints — results green.
ops-bot: marked two canary hosts for termination; new hosts spun up on stable revision.
maya_sre: starting short-term remediation runbook: - lock rollout policy to stricter thresholds for prefetch-enabled builds - add canary metric alarm for memory growth slope - add guardrail to disable prefetch_cache automatically if GC stalls > 3 in 5m.
sam_oncall: agreed. create follow-up ticket and assign to release team + runtime.
ryan_release: created TICKET-2184 "prefetch cache: guardrails + safer rollout" and added triage notes.
julie_support: status page update posted: "Degraded behavior observed in canary rollout; rollback completed; no broader customer impact."
sam_oncall: closing the page for on-call. handing to postmortem owners: @maya_sre and @ryan_release. If anything resurfaces, re-open. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
maya_sre: will take postmortem, capturing timelines, logs, and the quick mitigations we applied.
ryan_release: leaving a short deploy note in the release log: "rollback executed 1728374284 — prefetch_cache feature disabled for canary; follow-up TICKET-2184."
sam_oncall: oncall handoff at 08:00 to @next_oncall; I'm adding notes to rotation channel. Thread resolved.
